clue.text: Stormy until dark

indicators.note: stormy suggests turbulence, so the letters of the next word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A weather report: the storm will rage on until nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy' rearranges the letters of 'until'.
explanation.definitionFit: A room or street that is unlit has no lamps burning, so it is dark.

clue.text: Old pen carried upside down by Mozart, a classicist

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down says the concealed letters read from bottom to top
carried, completed by the later by, says the answer's letters are borne within the words that follow
by joins carried to name the words that bear the concealed letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A prison smuggled in, inverted, by a composer who was a classicist.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'carried' in the definition, but 'carried by' is what signals the concealment, so the definition is just 'Old pen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz was the notorious island prison in San Francisco Bay, closed in 1963, so it is an old pen.

clue.text: Cooked limes used principally for breakfast cereal

indicators.note: cooked hints at food being worked over, so these letters are mixed up
principally points to the leading letter of the word used

explanation.surface: A recipe note: lime pieces cooked and mainly used in a breakfast dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principally' takes U from 'used'; 'Cooked' shuffles it with LIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a Swiss-style mixture of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten in the morning.

clue.text: Five lost from barge in Oxford?

indicators.note: lost from says a letter is taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: to barge is to shove
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Seems to tell of five people falling off a punt or barge on the river at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barge' looks like a boat on the Isis but is the verb SHOVE; 'lost from' takes away V.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a style of lace-up leather shoe; the question mark flags it as one example.

clue.text: Country backing force during tricky gun fighting method

indicators.note: backing means the country's abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the other
tricky suggests the word gun is handled awkwardly into a new order

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A nation supports troops while a gun proves hard to handle in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' backing is the UK abbreviation; 'tricky' shuffles the gun's letters and 'during' places the force symbol among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Kung fu is a Chinese martial art, an unarmed way of fighting.

clue.text: Hold back army and strengthen with further support

parts.note: to rein in is to hold back
an army is a fighting force

explanation.surface: Military orders: restrain the army and send it backup troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce is to bolster something by adding extra men, material or bracing.

clue.text: Attack on way to introduce comedian

indicators.note: to introduce here means the street abbreviation takes another piece into its middle

parts.note: ST, street, a way
a comedian can be called a laugh, an entertaining person

explanation.surface: A compere launches a stand-up act as if mounting an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to introduce' means the street takes the comedian inside it; calling an entertaining person 'a laugh' is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce, overwhelming assault.

clue.text: Overthrow argument about Murphy, say

indicators.note: about signals turning the word round, back to front

parts.note: to rebut is to overthrow an argument by refuting it

explanation.surface: Someone disputes a point made about a person named Murphy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses REBUT. 'Murphy' is Irish-flavoured slang for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato, nicknamed a murphy, is a swollen underground stem, a typical example of the botanical category.

clue.text: Advanced inside information followed by heartless city operation

parts.note: GEN is slang for information, especially the inside facts

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle of the word city, leaving only its ends

explanation.surface: A spy story: secret intelligence leads to a raid on a soulless city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' keeps CY from 'city'; 'followed by' just orders the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Agency means action or operation, as in something happening through the agency of another.

clue.text: Not completely wrong eating during last series of exams

indicators.note: eating says one piece swallows another, taking it inside
not completely drops the final letter of the synonym

parts.note: wrong means false
during means in, as in the course of

explanation.surface: A student misbehaves, snacking in the middle of their final examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not completely' docks the last letter of the synonym for wrong, and 'eating' has it swallow the word for during.
explanation.definitionFit: Finals are the closing exams of a university degree course.

clue.text: Taking on and winning

definitions.meaning: ... means hiring or taking on staff, or ... an enemy

explanation.definitionFit: Engaging is both employing someone and having an attractive, appealing manner.

clue.text: Vehicle making a comeback in Nagasaki or Tokyo

indicators.note: making a comeback says the concealed letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words naming the Japanese cities

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A car returns to service in one of two Japanese cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but it is what signals the concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian carriage or sleigh drawn by three horses abreast.

clue.text: Regrettably adopting one false identity

indicators.note: adopting says the first piece takes the second into itself

parts.note: alas expresses regret
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Sadly someone has taken on a fake persona.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' puts I inside ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed name used to hide one's real identity.

clue.text: One's turn done with no restraints in cell

indicators.note: restraints are the outer edges holding each word in, so without them only the inner letters of each word remain

explanation.surface: A prisoner, having served the sentence, is freed from shackles in the cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no restraints' strips the first and last letter from each of 'One's', 'turn' and 'done', leaving NE, UR, ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is a nerve cell, the basic unit of the nervous system.

clue.text: Clothing for work in manure a discerning person turns over

parts.note: dung is manure

indicators.note: turns over in a down clue flips the following letters to read upwards

parts.note: a seer sees and perceives, a discerning person

explanation.surface: A farm worker in overalls turns over a heap of muck.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the discerning person 'turns over'; the 'a' stays in place before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are hard-wearing bib-and-brace overalls worn as workwear.

clue.text: Call large bird, not difficult in East London

indicators.note: not says the following piece is left out of the bird's name

parts.note: a buzzard is a large bird of prey
Cockneys drop the initial H, so hard becomes 'ard

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for a big bird in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the East London accent that drops H. 'not' removes 'ARD from BUZZARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a buzz is informal for phoning them, a call.

clue.text: With reserve in Mafia country when son's missing

indicators.note: missing means a letter is absent from the island's name

parts.note: Sicily is the homeland of the Mafia
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A Mafia family keeps its distance while one of the sons has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes the S from SICILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting icily is acting coldly, with aloofness and reserve.

clue.text: Following unlimited mounting pain, doctor in charge of feet

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means rising, so the letters read upwards
unlimited removes the bounding first and last letters

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: After growing pain, a doctor takes charge of someone's sore feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' leaves AI from 'pain' and 'mounting' turns it to IA. The feet are metrical feet in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambic describes verse built from iambs, the metrical foot of one short and one long syllable.

clue.text: Varying measure of old Canary wine

definitions.meaning: an old unit for goods such as wool or coal, its size varying by commodity
the old name for dry white fortified wine from Spain and the Canaries

explanation.definitionFit: Sack names both a historic bulk measure and the sherry-like wine Falstaff loved.

clue.text: Signal extreme distress about British Conservative's pitiful tale

indicators.note: about says the distress signal surrounds the next piece

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician cries for help, telling a sad story about Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the distress call round the abbreviation for British.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a sad account told to win sympathy.

clue.text: Poor game is discriminating against oldies

definitions.note: a participle phrase standing for the noun: the practice of discriminating against the old

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are badly arranged and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A shabby sport that shuts out older players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges GAMEIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is prejudice or unfair treatment on grounds of a person's age, particularly against the elderly.

clue.text: Undiminished in sensitivity for others

parts.note: tact is a delicate awareness of others' feelings

explanation.surface: A tribute to someone whose consideration for others has never faded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intact is whole and unharmed, with nothing taken away.

clue.text: Small, pudgy, squat and thick

explanation.definitionFit: Stubby describes something short and broad, like a stub of a pencil.

clue.text: US airline employing college rock fan in 50s

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
a Ted, Teddy boy, was a 1950s rock and roll fan in Britain

explanation.surface: An American carrier hires a student who loves rock and roll in his fifties.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style dress devoted to rock and roll; '50s' looks like an age.
explanation.definitionFit: United Airlines is one of the major American passenger carriers.

clue.text: Secret store of headgear used up round start of spring

indicators.note: round says the hat letters go around the next piece
used up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: hats are headgear

indicators.note: start of takes just the first letter of spring

explanation.surface: A hidden hoard of hats is used up at the start of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used up' turns HATS into STAH; 'round' puts S, from 'start of spring', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stash is a hidden supply put away for later.

clue.text: Irritable about university intake, principally, after good financial gift

indicators.note: after says this group comes behind the letter for good
about says the bad-tempered word goes around the following letters

parts.note: ratty means irritable

indicators.note: principally takes the leading letter of intake

explanation.surface: A grumpy remark about university admissions, after a generous donation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts U plus I, from 'intake, principally', inside RATTY; G goes in front because 'after' places it first.
explanation.definitionFit: A gratuity is a tip, a sum of money given voluntarily for service.

clue.text: Group of students indeed worry, at heart

parts.note: yea is an old word meaning yes, indeed

indicators.note: at heart takes the central letter of worry

explanation.surface: A class of pupils is truly anxious deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' takes R, the centre of 'worry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A school year is a cohort of pupils of the same age taught together.

clue.text: Entirely fashionable Wizard of Oz character

parts.note: in means fashionable
Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: A wholly stylish figure from The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for as a whole, completely.

clue.text: Fruit and vegetable, cold/hot

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A menu note: fruit with vegetables, served chilled or warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold/hot' is the tap pair C and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach is a soft, juicy stone fruit with downy skin.

clue.text: Barge in, upset at charges

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone storms in, angered by the fees being demanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges ATCHARGES.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to attend a party or event uninvited, pushing in.
